# S4: ecology, encounters and hazards (interface note)

Owner: Opus 5.5 high. Branch: `t3/a550755c` from baseline `6a0fa56`. These are new modules only; no B1 root was edited. The coordinator composes them after B1.

## What the player gets
Later regions get wildlife that reacts to what the player does. Each animal reacts to one main cue (lamp light, layer vibration or sustained noise), warns in stages, and can be avoided by changing behaviour, using terrain or habitat, or with a nonlethal tool. No animal can be killed and nothing in progression asks for it. The hazards (heat, brine, current, sediment, darkness and pressure bands) announce themselves before they harm, and each warning names its protection and where that protection's material starts.

## Interfaces the coordinator wires
```ts
// World access: today's sim/world.ts through ecologyWorldFrom(world, refuges); S1 supplies the same three calls.
interface EcologyWorld { waterY; floor(x,z); clearLine(a,b); refuges: {position, radius}[] }
stimulusFrom(s: GameState, loudness, { lamp, scanned? }): Stimulus   // loudness = step.ts's existing value
stepEcology(state: EcologyState, { tick, stimulus, protection, vehicleId, commands? }, world)
  -> { events: EcologyEvent[], effects: { diverHealth, vehicleHealth, drift: Vec3 /*m/s*/, visibility } }
protectionFor(hull | null, fitted: ProtectionId[]): Protection
ecologyView(state, tick, stimulus | null): EcologyView               // render, HUD and audio read only this
createCreatureLayer(scene, cel, parent?).update(view, seconds, camera)
pressureWarning(prevDepth, depth, rating): string | null             // legible bands over survival.ts pressure
parseEcology(raw, { vehicleIds })  /  resumeEcology(state)          // load: cross-check the fleet, then re-warn
```
Composition in `step.ts`: call `stepEcology` beside `updateThreat`, using the same loudness. Subtract `effects.diverHealth` and `effects.vehicleHealth` the way hunter bites are subtracted. Add `effects.drift * DT` to the actor's move delta before the solid sweep. Map the existing `distraction` command to `{type:"deploy", kind:"acoustic"}` as well. Events become notices: `ecology-cue` and `hazard-warning` go to the hazard channel with their caption, which is the text equivalent of the visual cue. `ecology-strike` becomes `threat-damage` for presentation only: apply health once, from `effects`. Map only a successful, paid `distraction` to an acoustic deploy at its real target. On loading a save, call `parseEcology(raw, { vehicleIds: fleet.vehicles.map(v => v.id) })` and then `resumeEcology(state)` once before the first step. Composition should also drive the existing renderer's school and scavenger cues from `EcologyView.schoolScattered` and `scavengers.retreat`. Today the roster is far outside the compact world, so the step is a measured no-op until S2 places the regions (see the integration test).

## Proposed persisted fields (one schema change at integration)
- `world.ecology = { agents[6], deterrents[≤6], diver: Exposure, hulls: ({id} & Exposure)[≤8] }`, where `Exposure = {heat, brine, heatWarned, brineWarned}`. Each `*Warned` field counts the seconds of the current warning episode.
  - Each agent stores `{id, mode, position, yaw, awareness, modeSeconds, cycles, refractory, cue, struck}` in roster order. A save and load mid-encounter resumes identically; this is tested.
  - Hull IDs follow the fleet save contract (`/^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,80}$/`) and are unique. With `vehicleIds` passed in, each must also exist in the same save.
  - The hulls are an array, not an object map, and the parser checks own properties only. `__proto__`, `constructor` and similar IDs are ordinary entries; this is tested from parse through a step and back.
- `player.lamp: boolean`, default true, toggled by a new `{type:"lamp"}` command.
- Items and recipes proposed for the registry: `glow_lure` ×2 (glass 1, resin 1), `startle_ink` ×2 (membrane 1, resin 1), `heat_shroud` and `brine_seals` as suit fittings, `hull_heat_lining`, `hull_brine_seals` and `trim_vanes` as hull modules. Costs are in `hazards.ts` and `equipment.ts`. Commands: `deploy-lure` and `release-ink`.
- Hazard cycles derive from the saved `tick`. Cue animals have no state.

## Threats (each warns at least 5 s before any lunge, and only one animal lunges at a time)
| Species, region | Senses | Warning ladder (pattern and posture, not hue alone) | Ways out without a tool | Tool counters | Counter material, first reachable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Glare stalker, Ember Rift warm passage | lamp light (strongest in the dark), some noise | a light run along the flank → paired pulses while closing → **lights dark, body straight** for the lunge → slow coil away | dim the lamp and keep still; climb to cool pale ledges (it cannot leave warm water) | glow lure (it follows); ink (it is blinded) | glass, resin and membrane: reef, isles and upper Canopy |
| Layer skate, Mirror Divide dense layer | vibration at the layer surface, some noise | the mirror dimples → a widening ripple tracks you → the layer bulges | cross slowly where the sails drift; climb more than about 4 m above the layer (it cannot follow) | ink | as above |
| Hollow choir, Meridian gallery (sessile colony) | sustained noise, lamp up close | the bells hum → they swell in unison → a pressure pulse inside 16 m | coast quietly (a Creel on quiet thrust, loudness 0.12, is never noticed); leave the reach | acoustic pulse elsewhere (it spends the chorus) | existing service tool and reserve cell |

The existing Canopy sound hunter is untouched.

## Ecological interactions (pure functions; they can never disagree with the rule they teach)
- **Ember mites** leave the chimney lip at least 5 s before every vent, and the caption says so.
- **Basin scavengers** back into their burrows before each sediment surge, and whenever loud machinery is near.
- **Brine sails** drift a calm lane more than 15 m above the layer, in under 0.25 m/s of current.
- **The Lantern school** scatters at noise the sound hunter can hear.

## Hazards
| Hazard and cue | Without protection | Protection (suit / hull) | Its material, first reachable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Split-chimney plume: 18 s vent every 75 s, preceded by the mites | warnings at 40%, 70% and 100%, then harm; the warm passage can be crossed at ordinary swim speed with no warning | ceramic heat shroud / hull heat lining; Mantle tolerates heat itself | pressure ceramic on the cool-flank lip (262 m), reached by the 350 m configuration, outside every field |
| Dense brine below the mirror layer | slowly etches suit or seals (1.5 HP/s after the 5 s warning lead), below the layer only | lattice brine seals / hull brine seals | brine lattice on the outer ledge (376 m), reached by the 450 m configuration, 34 m above the layer |
| Saddle downwelling: ribbons point down, grains streak | drift toward the layer: Hush 0.8 m/s, Mantle under 0.2 m/s | resin trim vanes | resin and alloy, early |
| Basin sediment surge: scavengers hide first | visibility down, slight drift | timing; step onto the ridge | none needed |
| Unlit passages and galleries | light-hunting animals see a lamp more readily | a lamp or not: the light-or-stealth trade-off | none |
| Pressure bands at 85%, 95% and 100% of rating | the existing survival damage | each caption names the next refit and its source region | per the expedition contract |

Tests check that each first deposit sits under 90% of its configuration's rating, is free of heat, brine and current over a full cycle, and is out of every animal's reach. Every protection and kit material comes from an earlier tier.

## Adverse case: cornered with no tool (`tests/ecology-adverse.test.ts`)
The crevice stays in place throughout, and the test counts every source of ecology health loss: strikes and field exposure.
- **Corner phase.** The diver holds station with the lamp at 0.6 and noise at 0.6, until every animal that engaged is resting in refractory.
- **Escape phase.** The diver swims out quietly at 2 m/s with the lamp still on, through an actual opening.
  - Velocity is reported truthfully and current drift is applied.
  - Movement is swept against the rock inflated by the 0.4 m diver radius, sliding along faces.
  - "Safe" means no field load and no animal able to reach the diver.

| Fixture and route | Disengaged | Safe | Total loss (strikes) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Rift stalker: mouth, then up out of the passage | 30.6 s | 43.1 s | **28.0** (28) |
| Rift stalker: reviewer's route along the passage | 30.6 s | 47.6 s | **28.0** (28) |
| Layer skate: up out of the brine at the layer | 25.5 s | 28.6 s | **45.6** (18) |
| Hollow choir: up out of the pulse reach | 40.1 s | 43.7 s | **18.0** (18) |

The documented bound is 60 HP. Nothing strikes during an escape. A diver who stays cornered and loud past the refractory window can start a new, again fully warned, engagement. A diver who goes dark and still at the first warning is never struck. Design changes behind these numbers:
- The warm passage drops from 0.42 to 0.36. Lingering builds load slowly and is fully warned.
- Brine is a slow equipment hazard: diver harm 1.5/s (was 4), hull 1/s (was 2), and a 1 m edge (was 2 m). Climbing a metre ends it.
- The skate withdraws in 4 s instead of 7.

## Warning lead and cover (tested invariants)
- Every lunge or pulse comes at least 5 s after its animal's first warning of that engagement. This is fuzzed over 18 wandering, flickering players.
- Hazard harm comes at least 5 s after the first warning of the episode. This holds for every harmful field, at four cycle phases, for the diver and every hull with and without protection, and when resumed from loads of 39–100 after `resumeEcology`.
- Mites and scavengers signal at least 5 s before each field starts rising.
- Contact needs a clear line from the animal to the diver. The choir's pulse needs a clear line from the bells; solid cover shelters completely. Layer vibration through rock is muffled like noise. The regressions cover the reviewer's skate wall, a stalker commit with cover inserted, and a choir with shelter compared with open water.

## Checks (all on this branch)
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- 35 pure tests (`tests/ecology-{agents,adverse,hazards,integration}.test.ts`), run with `node --test`: all pass.
- `tests/ecology-render.test.ts` through `heavy-check.sh` with `--test-concurrency=1` and 2 GiB: passes. Three rebuilds keep the same names and counts, dispose returns the scene to baseline and keeps the shared cel, rendering writes no state, and a lunge shows no lit vertices. The layer update cost 0.04–0.18 ms per frame for 91 meshes across runs.
- `vite build`: passes.
- The pure step costs about 24 µs with two active stalkers in open water; the real `lineOfSight` adapter will cost more.
- The viewer ran in the SwiftShader preview. Screenshots: `/work/tmp/s4/shots/*.png`; `plume-mites-on-lip.png` shows the mites re-anchored on the lip. The full suite was not run, because no existing file changed.

## Known limits
- Positions are provisional: the regions are not authored, so all of this runs in open water at proposed anchors. S2 should re-anchor `ECOLOGY_SITES` and rerun the deposit and reach tests.
- Animals use simple kinematic steering: `clearLine` checks plus habitat and territory clamps. There is no sweep against hull meshes like the hunter's. Contact uses a reach radius plus the actor radius.
- The art is a first pass: the stalker's segments are visible up close, and the skate reads best from above. The sails were too small in my test framing.
- Audio cue IDs are not mapped yet; S6 can key off `EcologyEvent.cue` and the species.
- All numbers are untested tuning. No human playtest has been done, and frame rate on the 3090 is unmeasured.
- Scope flags, design additions within owner scope:
  - a lamp switch as a stealth control;
  - two consumable nonlethal kits;
  - the one-lunge-at-a-time rule;
  - a 12 m refuge exclusion margin.
